# Copilot instructions — hsooligan95.github.io

You are working in Andrew Hsu's **developer site**: a static page that
presents his agent-platform portfolio — a fleet graph of the projects,
an agent ops feed that replays recorded runs as an agent group chat,
and a live tamper-evidence demo over a real hash-chained event store.

## Stack

- Plain HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript. No framework, no bundler,
  no build step — the files served are the files in this repo.
- `index.html`, `style.css`, `app.js` — the page itself.
- `canonical.js` — canonical JSON serialization matching the Python
  implementation used by agent-trace, so browser-side hashes agree
  byte-for-byte with the stored events.
- `data/` — project list, feed scripts, and tamper-demo data; the run
  data there is generated by `tools/`, not hand-written.

## Tests

```bash
python tools/verify_site.py         # full browser verification: graph, tamper demo, all three feed channels
node tools/verify_js_canonical.mjs  # browser canonicalization checked against the Python reference
```

## Architecture notes

- No external assets: no CDN scripts, fonts, or images. Everything the
  page needs ships in this repo.
- Positioning rule: no title-forward copy — no seniority claims, job
  titles, or years-of-experience boasts anywhere on the page. The
  projects speak for themselves.
- `canonical.js` must stay byte-compatible with the Python verifier in
  agent-trace: for the same event, both must produce identical
  canonical bytes and identical hashes. Any change to it is proven
  with `tools/verify_js_canonical.mjs`, not by inspection.
- `data/drill.js`, `data/chain.js`, and `data/feed.js` are generated
  artifacts. Regenerate them with `tools/gen_data.py` /
  `tools/gen_feed.py` from the source stores; never hand-edit them.
- Every number on the page (event counts, costs, scores) comes from a
  real recorded run. Never invent or round a figure for presentation.

## Shared rules

- Use Unix LF line endings in every file; never CRLF.
- Never commit secrets, tokens, or credentials — real or synthetic-looking.
- Tests must pass before you describe a change as complete; run the test
  command above and report honestly if you cannot.
- Prefer the smallest complete implementation: reuse what already exists in
  this repo before adding new code, files, or dependencies.
